bug_semantics: OliveTin's live execution-event delivery retained a subscriber or connection globally and fanned every action's execution-start, execution-finish, and output data to every recipient without checking that recipient's per-action view/log authorization. The completion payload exposed accumulated command output and the later chunk event exposed live bytes, allowing a low-privileged authenticated dashboard user to receive metadata and output for protected actions.
flaw_origin: Commit e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 first created the causal all-client output sink: internal/websocket/websocket.go registered every connection in a global clients slice, converted each completed InternalLogEntry including Stdout and Stderr, and broadcast it to every client without an action/user authorization decision. Its sole parent had an action-view ACL but only a passive websocket accept/read/close stub and no execution listener, output payload, client registry, or fan-out. Later commits added a Logs permission and live output chunks without filtering the broadcast. Commit a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 then carried the already-existing global event-fan-out design into the ConnectRPC EventStream during a 110-file 3k port/aggregate; it introduced a second vulnerable transport but was not the first causal writer. The legacy websocket path was filtered by 4e7273b616245d60626b51a291edd97ab8ef53bc, while the parallel EventStream remained vulnerable until acd6cb839e999bb2b0e9a91424f51e88be3f7ffc.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 shows human author and committer jamesread <contact@jread.com> and only the message 'feature: websocket implemenation at last!', with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, bot identity, or other AI attribution in the BIC commit object.
evidence: The bundled first-party advisory identifies the modern service/internal/api/api.go EventStream callbacks and documents a 3000.10.2 PoC in which an ACL-less alice receives an admin-started protected action's ExecutionFinished output. Its normalized package range '< 3000.10.2' and first-patched 3000.10.2 conflict with that PoC, so Git tag contents were used for the closing boundary.

The introducer disagreement was primary a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404/d4fe9eaa793f508f44bc60f0a1109cb008a6a5b0 versus reviewer e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3/6116e954ba5de9936463dbaf76f2e14aef6d9e72. git log --all --reverse -S'broadcast("ExecutionFinished", le)' --pickaxe-all -- internal/websocket/websocket.go returns e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 as the first addition, and git log -L over WebsocketExecutionListener.OnExecutionFinished traces the complete-output fan-out continuously back to that commit. git grep at e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 locates the global clients slice at line 18, OnExecutionFinished at line 38, Stdout/Stderr copies at lines 44-45, and the all-client WriteMessage loop at lines 82-83.

Direct-parent resolution: git cat-file -p e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 names 6116e954ba5de9936463dbaf76f2e14aef6d9e72 as its sole parent. git show 6116e954ba5de9936463dbaf76f2e14aef6d9e72:internal/httpservers/websocket.go shows only accept/read/close behavior, while git grep for IsAllowedView in that parent shows action authorization already existed in internal/acl/acl.go and grpcApiActions.go. Thus the unauthorized execution-output sink is absent in the direct parent, establishing introducer_parent_absent=true for the resolved BIC.

The primary candidate fails the vulnerability-level direct-parent and smallest-origin checks. git show --stat a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 reports a 110-file 3k progress aggregate, and git diff-tree -r --summary -M -C identifies service/internal/grpcapi/grpcApi.go to service/internal/api/api.go as a 41% rename. Although git blame -M -C -C attributes the new EventStream callback lines to a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404, git show d4fe9eaa793f508f44bc60f0a1109cb008a6a5b0:service/internal/websocket/websocket.go proves that its immediate parent already emitted the same EventExecutionStarted, EventExecutionFinished, and EventOutputChunk data, including Output, through an unconditional loop over all clients. Therefore a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 is a later parallel transport port/reimplementation, not the first causal BIC; the reviewer's SHA and parent win both assigned disputes.

Lifecycle checks support the resolved origin: git show --stat db5de9be9793be65e2a77ab71656713f97bc779b adds the Logs permission and filters grpc log retrieval but does not touch websocket.go; git show ac0f3ab6f8346157b1b2a47737ef237e0ae3af8f adds OnOutputChunk and calls the same unfiltered broadcast; and git show 4e7273b616245d60626b51a291edd97ab8ef53bc adds acl.IsAllowedLogs filtering only in service/internal/httpservers/websocket.go, not the parallel ConnectRPC EventStream.

Direct fix verification: git show acd6cb839e999bb2b0e9a91424f51e88be3f7ffc -- service/internal/api/api.go shows mayViewExecutionEvent delegating to isLogEntryAllowed and guards before delivery of execution-start, execution-finish, and output-chunk events. The commit subject directly names GHSA-228v-wc5r-j8m7 and its patch includes the corresponding API regression tests, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are both acd6cb839e999bb2b0e9a91424f51e88be3f7ffc.

Version-boundary verification: git tag --contains e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 --sort=version:refname begins at 2023.10.09 and includes every 3000 release through the advisory's demonstrated 3000.10.2. git tag --contains acd6cb839e999bb2b0e9a91424f51e88be3f7ffc --sort=version:refname begins at 3000.11.3; git merge-base with 3000.11.2 is b298a6bd8caadd8a69eeb731771f5ac659b9e237, while with 3000.11.3 it is the fix itself. git grep shows 3000.11.2 has the unguarded callbacks and 3000.11.3 has mayViewExecutionEvent checks, establishing last vulnerable 3000.11.2 and first fixed 3000.11.3.

BIC-only AI check: git cat-file -p e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 shows tree 7cc37013df7a695005dcf36fa524fc89f2e5d48f, sole parent 6116e954ba5de9936463dbaf76f2e14aef6d9e72, human author/committer jamesread <contact@jread.com>, and only the subject 'feature: websocket implemenation at last!'. There is no canonical AI attribution signal. The chosen BIC is a direct single-parent commit rather than a move or squash aggregate, so no decomposition is claimed.
reasoning: Vulnerability-first history resolves both assigned disagreements in favor of the reviewer. The primary correctly identified when the specific ConnectRPC EventStream lines appeared, but treated endpoint absence as vulnerability absence. The required direct-parent check is causal: a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404's parent already had the same live execution-event and complete-output disclosure through a global all-client broadcaster. The earlier e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 is the smallest ordinary commit that first wrote that sink, and its parent truly lacks it while already containing action-view authorization. Subsequent ACL, output-chunk, 3k transport-port, and partial websocket-fix commits preserve a continuous flaw lifecycle until the advisory's direct EventStream correction. Release ancestry verifies the effective first fixed version as 3000.11.3 despite inconsistent advisory package metadata. Because the resolved BIC and direct fix are verified and the BIC commit object contains no AI attribution, the gate-complete verdict is NOT_AI.
